key_insight: pUniFind is a single, large-scale multimodal deep learning model that unifies peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing, trained on >100 million spectra to substantially improve peptide identification and modification discovery.
problem_solved: Mass-spectrometry peptide interpretation is fragmented across separate database-search and de novo tools, limiting sensitivity for novel peptides and post-translational modifications; pUniFind addresses this by providing a unified, scalable model that handles both tasks and discovers modifications more reliably.
method: Train a large multimodal model on >100 million spectra paired with peptide sequences and metadata to learn joint spectrum–sequence representations.
Unify peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing in one architecture so the same model can score database matches and generate novel peptide sequences (including modified residues).
Leverage multimodal pretraining and task-specific fine-tuning (scoring + sequence-generation objectives) to improve identification accuracy and modification discovery.
impact: Demonstrates that scaling multimodal deep learning in a scientific domain yields practical gains—reducing the need for separate pipelines and enabling more accurate, modification-aware peptide discovery—offering a template for unified models in other measurement-driven fields.
visual_elements: Model schematic: multimodal encoder (spectra + metadata) feeding a joint decoder for scoring and sequence generation.
Bar chart comparing peptide identification rates and modification discovery vs. leading baseline tools.
Pipeline comparison: unified pUniFind workflow vs. traditional split database-search + de novo flowchart.
Heatmap or scatter showing types/frequencies of newly discovered modifications and confidence scores.
paper_title: A large-scale unified deep learning model for peptide mass spectrum interpretation trained on multimodal data
paper_authors: Jiale Zhao, Pengzhi Mao, Kaifei Wang, Yiming Li, Yaping Peng
